title: The rise of esports
paragraphs: There are many ways we can enjoy sport – watching it on TV or a smartphone, attending an event at a stadium or even playing the game. But for those who enjoy getting competitive with their computer gaming, there are realistic-looking games with lifelike graphics to be played without leaving home. It’s this type of sport – if that’s what we can call it – that has become big business. And interest in it has gone to a new level.

Initially, grabbing a joystick or controller and playing a game was a solitary activity. But around 20 years ago computers became cheaper and the internet became faster, which made it much easier for more people to get involved with computer gaming. This led to gamers connecting with each other around the world, so they could go head-to-head online. It also became a spectator sport, with people watching others play. The whole experience has been given the name ‘esports’ – electronic sports.

Now, huge esports tournaments take place all over the world in big arenas with large crowds. Die-hard enthusiasts, who have become first-rate players, are now well-known - some play together in teams. Its top stars can earn millions of dollars a year, without even breaking into a sweat! And fans from around the world tune in to watch the action online. The global audience is now estimated at more than 200 million and growing. Annual revenues from esports, currently around 650 million dollars for events, continue to rise with billions more generated through video games sales.

Famous football clubs are now trying to get in on the action. England’s Football Association for example launched its first esports team this year, known as the eLions. It recruited Fifa 19 players to represent them at the inaugural Fifa eNations Cup. Mark Bullingham, the FA's chief commercial and football development officer, said "The FA prides itself on being a modern, innovative organisation that strives to engage and inspire all generations of football fans."

But while this virtual version of football might give aspiring footballers a chance to get closer to the real game, some might argue the lack of physical activity means it shouldn’t be called a sport – and the biggest winners are the companies who promote and sell esports.

vocabulary.entry: lifelike graphics /ˈlaɪflaɪk ˈɡræfɪks/ 逼真的画面
vocabulary.example: The lifelike graphics of this game make players feel like they are in a real world.
vocabulary.translation: 这款游戏逼真的画面让玩家仿佛置身真实世界。

vocabulary.entry: big business /bɪɡ ˈbɪznəs/ 庞大的产业；大生意
vocabulary.example: Online education has become big business in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来，在线教育已经发展成一项庞大的产业。

vocabulary.entry: joystick /ˈdʒɔɪstɪk/ n. 游戏摇杆
vocabulary.example: He prefers using a joystick rather than a mouse to play racing games.
vocabulary.translation: 玩赛车游戏时，他更喜欢用游戏摇杆而非鼠标。

vocabulary.entry: controller /kənˈtrəʊlə(r)/ n. 游戏手柄
vocabulary.example: The new wireless controller is more comfortable to hold for long gaming sessions.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新款无线游戏手柄长时间握持也很舒适。

vocabulary.entry: solitary /ˈsɒlətri/ adj. 单独的；独自的
vocabulary.example: Reading is a solitary activity that brings me a lot of peace.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读是一项能给我带来内心平静的独处活动。

vocabulary.entry: get involved with /ɡet ɪnˈvɒlvd wɪð/ 参与；涉足
vocabulary.example: More and more young people are getting involved with volunteer work.
vocabulary.translation: 越来越多的年轻人开始参与志愿工作。

vocabulary.entry: go head-to-head /ɡəʊ hed tə hed/ 正面交锋；对决
vocabulary.example: The two top teams will go head-to-head in the final next week.
vocabulary.translation: 两支顶尖队伍将在下周的决赛中正面交锋。

vocabulary.entry: spectator sport /spekˈteɪtə spɔːt/ 观赏性体育运动
vocabulary.example: Football is one of the most popular spectator sports around the world.
vocabulary.translation: 足球是全球最受欢迎的观赏性体育运动之一。

vocabulary.entry: esports /ˈiːspɔːts/ n. 电子竞技
vocabulary.example: Esports has become a global phenomenon among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 电子竞技已经成为年轻人中的全球性热潮。

vocabulary.entry: tournament /ˈtʊənəmənt/ n. 锦标赛；赛事
vocabulary.example: He won the gold medal in the international chess tournament.
vocabulary.translation: 他在国际象棋锦标赛中赢得了金牌。

vocabulary.entry: arena /əˈriːnə/ n. 大型场馆；竞技场
vocabulary.example: The basketball game will be held in a newly built arena downtown.
vocabulary.translation: 这场篮球赛将在市中心新建的大型场馆举行。

vocabulary.entry: die-hard enthusiast /ˌdaɪ hɑːd ɪnˈθjuːziæst/ 铁杆爱好者；忠实粉丝
vocabulary.example: Die-hard enthusiasts of the band queued for hours to buy concert tickets.
vocabulary.translation: 这支乐队的铁杆粉丝排了好几个小时的队购买演唱会门票。

vocabulary.entry: first-rate /ˌfɜːst ˈreɪt/ adj. 一流的；顶尖的
vocabulary.example: The hotel offers first-rate service and comfortable rooms.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店提供一流的服务和舒适的客房。

vocabulary.entry: break into a sweat /breɪk ˈɪntu ə swet/ 出汗；费力
vocabulary.example: He didn't break into a sweat even after running five kilometers.
vocabulary.translation: 他跑了五公里后，竟然一滴汗都没出。

vocabulary.entry: tune in /tjuːn ɪn/ 收看；收听
vocabulary.example: Millions of people tuned in to watch the royal wedding live.
vocabulary.translation: 数百万人收看了这场皇室婚礼的直播。

vocabulary.entry: revenue /ˈrevənjuː/ n. 收入；收益
vocabulary.example: The company's annual revenue increased by 20% last year.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司去年的年收入增长了20%。

vocabulary.entry: get in on the action /ɡet ɪn ɒn ði ˈækʃn/ 参与其中；加入热潮
vocabulary.example: Many small businesses are trying to get in on the action of the online shopping boom.
vocabulary.translation: 许多小企业都想投身网购热潮，分一杯羹。

vocabulary.entry: recruit /rɪˈkruːt/ v. 招募；招收
vocabulary.example: The company plans to recruit 50 new employees this year.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司计划今年招募50名新员工。

vocabulary.entry: inaugural /ɪˈnɔːɡjərəl/ adj. 首次的；创始的
vocabulary.example: The inaugural meeting of the club will be held next Monday.
vocabulary.translation: 该俱乐部的成立大会将于下周一举行。

vocabulary.entry: pride oneself on /praɪd wʌnˈself ɒn/ 以……为荣；为……感到自豪
vocabulary.example: She prides herself on being able to speak three languages fluently.
vocabulary.translation: 她为自己能流利地说三种语言而感到自豪。

vocabulary.entry: aspiring /əˈspaɪərɪŋ/ adj. 有抱负的；渴望成功的
vocabulary.example: Aspiring musicians from all over the country attended the competition.
vocabulary.translation: 来自全国各地的怀揣梦想的音乐人都参加了这场比赛。

vocabulary.entry: virtual /ˈvɜːtʃuəl/ adj. 虚拟的
vocabulary.example: Many people enjoy shopping in virtual stores on the internet.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人喜欢在网上的虚拟商店购物。

sentences.english: There are many ways we can enjoy sport – watching it on TV or a smartphone, attending an event at a stadium or even playing the game.
sentences.chinese: 我们有很多种享受体育运动的方式——在电视或智能手机上观看赛事、去体育场亲临现场观赛，甚至亲自上场参与。

sentences.english: But for those who enjoy getting competitive with their computer gaming, there are realistic-looking games with lifelike graphics to be played without leaving home.
sentences.chinese: 但对于那些喜欢在电脑游戏中一较高下的人来说，足不出户就能玩到画面逼真、场景写实的游戏。

sentences.english: It’s this type of sport – if that’s what we can call it – that has become big business. And interest in it has gone to a new level.
sentences.chinese: 正是这类活动——如果我们能将其称作体育运动的话——已经发展成了一项庞大的产业，人们对它的关注度也达到了全新高度。

sentences.english: Initially, grabbing a joystick or controller and playing a game was a solitary activity.
sentences.chinese: 最初，手握游戏摇杆或手柄打游戏还是一项单人活动。

sentences.english: But around 20 years ago computers became cheaper and the internet became faster, which made it much easier for more people to get involved with computer gaming.
sentences.chinese: 但大约20年前，电脑价格下降，网络速度提升，这让更多人更容易地参与电脑游戏。

sentences.english: This led to gamers connecting with each other around the world, so they could go head-to-head online.
sentences.chinese: 这使得全球的玩家能够相互联接，在线上展开对决。

sentences.english: It also became a spectator sport, with people watching others play.
sentences.chinese: 同时，观看他人打游戏也成了一项观赏性活动。

sentences.english: The whole experience has been given the name ‘esports’ – electronic sports.
sentences.chinese: 这种全新的体验被命名为“电子竞技”。

sentences.english: Now, huge esports tournaments take place all over the world in big arenas with large crowds.
sentences.chinese: 如今，大型电子竞技赛事在全球各地的大型场馆举办，现场座无虚席。

sentences.english: Die-hard enthusiasts, who have become first-rate players, are now well-known - some play together in teams.
sentences.chinese: 那些痴迷电竞的爱好者蜕变成了顶尖选手，如今已经声名远扬——部分选手还组建了战队并肩作战。

sentences.english: Its top stars can earn millions of dollars a year, without even breaking into a sweat!
sentences.chinese: 电竞领域的顶级明星每年能赚数百万美元，而且全程毫不费力！

sentences.english: And fans from around the world tune in to watch the action online.
sentences.chinese: 全球的粉丝都会在线收看赛事直播。

sentences.english: The global audience is now estimated at more than 200 million and growing.
sentences.chinese: 目前，电竞的全球观众数量估计已超过2亿，并且还在持续增长。

sentences.english: Annual revenues from esports, currently around 650 million dollars for events, continue to rise with billions more generated through video games sales.
sentences.chinese: 电竞赛事的年收入目前约为6.5亿美元，这一数字仍在上升，此外视频游戏销售还能带来数十亿美元的额外收入。

sentences.english: Famous football clubs are now trying to get in on the action.
sentences.chinese: 知名足球俱乐部如今也纷纷涉足电竞领域。

sentences.english: England’s Football Association for example launched its first esports team this year, known as the eLions.
sentences.chinese: 例如，英格兰足球总会今年成立了首支电竞战队，名为“电子雄狮队”。

sentences.english: It recruited Fifa 19 players to represent them at the inaugural Fifa eNations Cup.
sentences.chinese: 该协会招募了《FIFA 19》的玩家，代表球队参加首届国际足联电竞国家杯。

sentences.english: Mark Bullingham, the FA's chief commercial and football development officer, said "The FA prides itself on being a modern, innovative organisation that strives to engage and inspire all generations of football fans."
sentences.chinese: 英格兰足总首席商务与足球发展官马克·布林厄姆表示：“英格兰足总始终以自身是一个现代化、富有创新精神的组织为荣，我们致力于吸引并激励每一代足球迷。”

sentences.english: But while this virtual version of football might give aspiring footballers a chance to get closer to the real game, some might argue the lack of physical activity means it shouldn’t be called a sport – and the biggest winners are the companies who promote and sell esports.
sentences.chinese: 尽管这种虚拟足球能让怀揣足球梦的人们离真实的足球赛事更近一步，但有些人认为，电竞缺乏身体运动，因此不应被归类为体育运动——而最大的赢家其实是那些推广和经营电竞产业的公司。
